events.title: Junger BDSM Stammtisch Potsdam (18-34 J.)
events.description: Herzlich Willkommen an alle Kinkliebenden und Kinkneugierigen im <em><strong>Alter von 18 bis 34 Jahren</strong></em>.    <strong>Wer sind wir?</strong>    Wir sind ein Stammtisch zum Sozialisieren und Austauschen.    Im Kink-Bereich ist es unerlässlich, dass man sich frei über seine Vorlieben, Wünsche, Vorstellungen und auch Ängste oder Fragen mit Gleichgesinnten austauschen kann. Wir möchten dafür einen Safe-Space bieten, der frei von Vorurteilen, Kink-Shaming und Stigmatisierung ist. Wir sind ein <em><strong>explizit LGBTQAI+-freundlicher Ort</strong></em> . Rassistische, sexistische, homophobe und diskriminierende Aussagen oder Verhaltensweisen jedweder Art sind nicht willkommen!    <strong>Wann und wo treffen wir uns?</strong>    Gewöhnlich jeden <strong>dritten Donnerstag des Monats, ab 19 Uhr im Archiv in Potsdam (neue Location ab November 2025).</strong>    Hinweis: Hier sind die Preise auch studierenden-freundlich und du kannst dich mit einem Bierchen oder einer schönen Tasse heißer Schokolade dazu gesellen. Es gibt aber keinen Konsumzwang. Und leider ist es nicht barrierefrei.    Einen Dresscode gibt es nicht.    <strong>Was machen Wir?</strong>    Vor allem miteinander reden. Egal, ob schon seit vielen Jahren im Kink Bereich unterwegs, gerade erst herausgefunden, dass die Vorstellung von Fesseln einem eventuell gefallen könnte oder einfach nur interessiert, wir freuen uns auf dich. Sexuelle Spiele gibt es hier aber nicht, bei uns kannst du nur Gleichgesinnte finden, um euch dann gemeinsam wo anders auszuleben.    Bei Fragen oder Unsicherheiten kannst du an <a href="mailto:junger-bdsm-stammtisch@gmx.de" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">junger-bdsm-stammtisch@gmx.de</a> schreiben.    <strong>Unter 18 Jahren – was nun ?</strong>  Wenn du unter 18 bist und Interesse am Thema BDSM und Kinks hast, dann wende dich an die <a class="underline text-inherit hover:text-inherit" href="https://smjg.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">SMJG</a>, die sind der perfekte Anlaufpunkt dafür.    Wir freuen uns, dich willkommen zu heißen und dich kennenzulernen.         Mehr Informationen findest du unter <a href="https://bdsm-potsdam.de/bdsm-stammtisch-potsdam/bdsm-stammtisch-potsdam-der-junge-stammtisch-laedt-ein/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">https://bdsm-potsdam.de/bdsm-stammtisch-potsdam/bdsm-stammtisch-potsdam-der-junge-stammtisch-laedt-ein/</a>,  <a href="https://bdsm-potsdam.de/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">https://bdsm-potsdam.de/</a> oder auf Instagram / Facebook.    Informiert euch bitte über die Website, E-Mail etc. vorher, ob Ort und Zeitpunkt nicht kurzfristig verändert werden mussten.

events.title: Rope Jam @Daruma
events.description: The Rope Jam at Daruma welcomes people of all levels and backgrounds to practice, play, chat, or just to watch.    Beginners and curious newcomers are super welcome, and you don’t need to come with a partner in order to attend.    We have a large 100sqm room, with a huge suspension frame, 10 Hashira, tea, and a cosy chill out area.    Tickets:  <strong><a href="https://www.daruma.berlin/all-events" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Browse the calendar, find the Jam and reserve a spot</a></strong>    The Rope Jam at Daruma is very often fully booked - often with a waiting list - and we don't like to allow in more people than we really have space for as it makes a less enjoyable tying experience for everyone. Therefore to attend you need to reserve a space using the link above. Remember to use cancel as soon as possible (using the link emailed to you when you signed up) if you are unable to attend as this frees up space for anyone who might be on the waiting list.    Price: 10€ regular / 5€ low income / 15€ supporter  The booking system does not take payments – you can pay in cash on the door according to what you can afford. We don’t ask for proof of low income, nor do we keep a record of who is paying what.    <strong>Instructions</strong>  Please arrive between 7pm and 7.30pm, after that the door will be closed. At 7.30pm, there is a short welcome round/introductory talk. If you are coming for the first time, we recommend you arrive in time for this. If you need to arrive later than 7.30pm, please send a message in advance to let us know as, in order to keep the space calm and quiet, it will no longer be possible to ring the doorbell.

events.title: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT SUMMERCONCERTS DAY1:<br>JAZZ VERSUS SOCCER<br>Hanno Busch<br>«Perspective»<br>Album Release Concert<br>Feat: Mathew Halpin-Claus Fischer-Jonas Burgwinkel
events.description:
Hanno Busch
«Perspective»
Album Release Concert
Feat: Mathew Halpin-Claus Fischer-Jonas Burgwinkel

Mit Perspective veröffentlicht der Gitarrist & Komponist Hanno Busch sein neues Album – ein vielschichtiges Werk, das musikalisch den Puls unserer Gegenwart einfängt. Gemeinsam mit seinem hochkarätig besetzten Quartett – Matthew Halpin, Jonas Burgwinkel und Claus Fischer – gelingt es Busch, komplexe Emotionen zwischen Kontemplation und Aufruhr, zwischen innerer Ruhe und drängender Unruhe in Klang zu übersetzen.
Nach seinem mit dem Echo Jazz ausgezeichneten Album Share This Room (Frutex Tracks, 2017) zeigt sich Busch auf Perspective erneut als sensibler Klangforscher. Seine neuen Kompositionen reflektieren den Wandel der Zeit – eine Ära geprägt von Effizienz, rascher Kommunikation und zugleich einem Mangel Empathie und Neugier auf echten Perspektivwechsel. In dieser Welt des ständigen Reagierens stellt Busch die Frage: Was passiert, wenn wir wirklich zuhören?

Das Zusammenspiel der vier Musiker ist ein Dialog auf Augenhöhe – offen, empathisch, kraftvoll. Improvisation wird hier zur Haltung, die das Spannungsfeld zwischen individueller Freiheit und kollektiver Verantwortung hörbar macht. Die Musik auf Perspective bewegt sich zwischen Jazz und zeitgenössischem Pop, lässt Raum für Stille und eruptive Energie, für Meditation und Aufruhr. Dabei bewahrt sie stets eine emotionale Klarheit, die berührt.

Perspective erscheint als liebevoll gestaltete LP, deren Artwork von Daniel F. Hirth an die handgefertigten Papierkunstwerke von Share This Room und Absent anschließt. Ein Album, das nicht nur musikalisch, sondern auch visuell konsequent zur Idee des Perspektivwechsels einlädt.

Im März 2026 wurde Busch’s Arbeit mit dem WDR Jazzpreis gewürdigt.

Mathew Halpin – Tenor & Soprano Saxophone, Flute
Claus Fischer – Bass
Jonas Burgwinkel – Drums

events.title: Meinberg/Greve/Wesley
events.description:
Lajos Meinberg grew up in a family of musicians, which nurtured his love for jazz from an early age. Since 2020, he has been studying at the Jazz Institute Berlin under Wolfgang Köhler, Tino Dorado, and Bastian Stein, and has been actively involved in the Berlin jazz scene since then. He has had the opportunity to perform with musicians such as Rodney Green, Doug Weiss, Matt Wilson and Martin Wind. Lajos received the Ingolf Burkhardt Award in 2022 and won first prize at the International Jazzhaus Piano Competition in Freiburg in 2024, as well as second prize at the International Jazz Piano Competition Lausanne in 2025. In August 2023, Lajos was part of the Elbphilharmonie Jazz Academy, where he had the chance to learn from musicians like Anat Cohen, Donny McCaslin, and Sullivan Fortner.
Johann Greve is a double bassist and composer from Lower Saxony. Since moving to Berlin in 2019, he has worked as a sideman on a wide variety of projects and established himself in the young Berlin jazz scene. He has performed with Percy Pursglove, Julius Gawlik, Charlotte Greve and Olga Reznichenko, among others. In March 2024, he recorded material for his debut album with his quartet.
California-born drummer Genius Wesley is an emerging force on the international jazz scene, known for his electrifying energy, deep musicality, and fearless improvisation. A prodigy percussionist, he has already performed with jazz greats such as David Binney, Sean Jones, Buster Williams, Azar Lawrence, Gerald Clayton, and many more.

events.title: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT SUMMERCONCERTS DAY2:<br>JAZZ VERSUS SOCCER<br>Hanno Busch<br>«Perspective»<br>Album Release Concert<br>Feat: Mathew Halpin-Claus Fischer-Jonas Burgwinkel
events.description:
Hanno Busch
«Perspective»
Album Release Concert
Feat: Mathew Halpin-Claus Fischer-Jonas Burgwinkel

Mit Perspective veröffentlicht der Gitarrist & Komponist Hanno Busch sein neues Album – ein vielschichtiges Werk, das musikalisch den Puls unserer Gegenwart einfängt. Gemeinsam mit seinem hochkarätig besetzten Quartett – Matthew Halpin, Jonas Burgwinkel und Claus Fischer – gelingt es Busch, komplexe Emotionen zwischen Kontemplation und Aufruhr, zwischen innerer Ruhe und drängender Unruhe in Klang zu übersetzen.
Nach seinem mit dem Echo Jazz ausgezeichneten Album Share This Room (Frutex Tracks, 2017) zeigt sich Busch auf Perspective erneut als sensibler Klangforscher. Seine neuen Kompositionen reflektieren den Wandel der Zeit – eine Ära geprägt von Effizienz, rascher Kommunikation und zugleich einem Mangel Empathie und Neugier auf echten Perspektivwechsel. In dieser Welt des ständigen Reagierens stellt Busch die Frage: Was passiert, wenn wir wirklich zuhören?

Das Zusammenspiel der vier Musiker ist ein Dialog auf Augenhöhe – offen, empathisch, kraftvoll. Improvisation wird hier zur Haltung, die das Spannungsfeld zwischen individueller Freiheit und kollektiver Verantwortung hörbar macht. Die Musik auf Perspective bewegt sich zwischen Jazz und zeitgenössischem Pop, lässt Raum für Stille und eruptive Energie, für Meditation und Aufruhr. Dabei bewahrt sie stets eine emotionale Klarheit, die berührt.

Perspective erscheint als liebevoll gestaltete LP, deren Artwork von Daniel F. Hirth an die handgefertigten Papierkunstwerke von Share This Room und Absent anschließt. Ein Album, das nicht nur musikalisch, sondern auch visuell konsequent zur Idee des Perspektivwechsels einlädt.

Im März 2026 wurde Busch’s Arbeit mit dem WDR Jazzpreis gewürdigt.

Hanno Busch – Guitar, Composition
Mathew Halpin – Tenor & Soprano Saxophone, Flute
Claus Fischer – Bass
Jonas Burgwinkel – Drums

events.title: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT SUMMERCONCERTS DAY3:<br>JAZZ VERSUS SOCCER<br>Hanno Busch<br>«Perspective»<br>Album Release Concert<br>Feat: Mathew Halpin-Claus Fischer-Jonas Burgwinkel
events.description:
Hanno Busch
«Perspective»
Album Release Concert
Feat: Mathew Halpin-Claus Fischer-Jonas Burgwinkel

Mit Perspective veröffentlicht der Gitarrist & Komponist Hanno Busch sein neues Album – ein vielschichtiges Werk, das musikalisch den Puls unserer Gegenwart einfängt. Gemeinsam mit seinem hochkarätig besetzten Quartett – Matthew Halpin, Jonas Burgwinkel und Claus Fischer – gelingt es Busch, komplexe Emotionen zwischen Kontemplation und Aufruhr, zwischen innerer Ruhe und drängender Unruhe in Klang zu übersetzen.
Nach seinem mit dem Echo Jazz ausgezeichneten Album Share This Room (Frutex Tracks, 2017) zeigt sich Busch auf Perspective erneut als sensibler Klangforscher. Seine neuen Kompositionen reflektieren den Wandel der Zeit – eine Ära geprägt von Effizienz, rascher Kommunikation und zugleich einem Mangel Empathie und Neugier auf echten Perspektivwechsel. In dieser Welt des ständigen Reagierens stellt Busch die Frage: Was passiert, wenn wir wirklich zuhören?

Das Zusammenspiel der vier Musiker ist ein Dialog auf Augenhöhe – offen, empathisch, kraftvoll. Improvisation wird hier zur Haltung, die das Spannungsfeld zwischen individueller Freiheit und kollektiver Verantwortung hörbar macht. Die Musik auf Perspective bewegt sich zwischen Jazz und zeitgenössischem Pop, lässt Raum für Stille und eruptive Energie, für Meditation und Aufruhr. Dabei bewahrt sie stets eine emotionale Klarheit, die berührt.

Perspective erscheint als liebevoll gestaltete LP, deren Artwork von Daniel F. Hirth an die handgefertigten Papierkunstwerke von Share This Room und Absent anschließt. Ein Album, das nicht nur musikalisch, sondern auch visuell konsequent zur Idee des Perspektivwechsels einlädt.

Im März 2026 wurde Busch’s Arbeit mit dem WDR Jazzpreis gewürdigt.

events.title: Rope Lab: Play & Connection - pain
events.description:
This is our experimental shibari playground for all skill levels. Each month explores a new topic — from shame and semenawa to performance, advanced movement, or the mythical “3rd rope” in TKs. We rotate between two themes, always bringing new inspiration to your rope practice. Open to all levels with foundational knowledge. Bring your curiosity, your questions, and your rope. 
This month we are focusing on: pain – weather you call it s/m or semenawa, this class is all about exploring how to use rope to create pain. We will explore both external pain and uncomfortable body positions. This class is suitable for all skill levels. 
Play & Connection
These classes are dedicated to the research of the interpersonal, connective, and fun side of shibari. Forget about rope technique for a while and learn hands-on skills for actually playing with what you know. The topic varies from month to month, and can be anything from pain and predicament ties to fun games like rope fight club. Come learn the skills that take your sessions from good to fantastic!

events.title: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT SUMMERWEEKCONCERTS DAY1:<br>JAZZ VERSUS SOCCER<br>Maria Baptist Trio<br>Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests<br>FEAT TODAY: Fabian Timm-Heinz Lichius
events.description:
Maria Baptist Trio
Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests
FEAT TODAY: Fabian Timm-Heinz Lichius

Maria Baptist gehört zu den profiliertesten Pianistinnen und Komponistinnen des zeitgenössischen Jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur nennt sie »eine der großen Jazzmusikerinnen aus Deutschland«, All About Jazz beschreibt ihren Klavierstil als »unendlich intelligent und stilvoll«. Sie wurde fünf Mal für den Preis der Deutschen Schallplattenkritik nominiert, darunter für Soloklavier-, Kammerjazz- und Jazzorchester-Produktionen.

Ein zentraler Bezugspunkt ihrer Musik ist das Trio mit Fabian Timm am Bass und Heinz Lichius am Schlagzeug. Hier ist im kleinen Format das Großorchestrale ihres Werkkatalogs hörbar: Kompositionen fließen ineinander, formen suitenhafte Rahmen, weite Spannungsbögen wechseln zwischen Intimität und Kraft, Improvisationen durchziehen die Stücke und verweben sich mit dem Material.

In der Reihe Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests spielt das Trio zunächst zwei Konzerte. Danach erweitert Maria Baptist die Besetzung jeweils an einem eigenen Abend mit Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger und Jan von Klewitz.
—
Maria Baptist is one of the most distinctive pianists and composers in contemporary jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur refers to her as “one of Germany’s greatest jazz musicians,” while All About Jazz describes her piano style as “infinitely clever and classy.“ She has been nominated five times for the German Record Critics’ Award, including solo piano, chamber jazz, and jazz orchestra productions.

A central focus of her music is the trio with Fabian Timm on bass and Heinz Lichius on drums. Here, the orchestral dimension of her music becomes audible in a small format: compositions flow into one another, forming suite-like structures; extended arcs of tension move between intimacy and power; improvisations run through the pieces and intertwine with the written material.

As part of the series Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests, the trio opens with two concerts. Maria Baptist then expands the ensemble on separate evenings with Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger and Jan von Klewitz.

events.description:
Maria Baptist Trio
Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests
FEAT TODAY: Fabian Timm-Heinz Lichius

Maria Baptist gehört zu den profiliertesten Pianistinnen und Komponistinnen des zeitgenössischen Jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur nennt sie »eine der großen Jazzmusikerinnen aus Deutschland«, All About Jazz beschreibt ihren Klavierstil als »unendlich intelligent und stilvoll«. Sie wurde fünf Mal für den Preis der Deutschen Schallplattenkritik nominiert, darunter für Soloklavier-, Kammerjazz- und Jazzorchester-Produktionen.

Ein zentraler Bezugspunkt ihrer Musik ist das Trio mit Fabian Timm am Bass und Heinz Lichius am Schlagzeug. Hier ist im kleinen Format das Großorchestrale ihres Werkkatalogs hörbar: Kompositionen fließen ineinander, formen suitenhafte Rahmen, weite Spannungsbögen wechseln zwischen Intimität und Kraft, Improvisationen durchziehen die Stücke und verweben sich mit dem Material.

In der Reihe Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests spielt das Trio zunächst zwei Konzerte. Danach erweitert Maria Baptist die Besetzung jeweils an einem eigenen Abend mit Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger und Jan von Klewitz.
—
Maria Baptist is one of the most distinctive pianists and composers in contemporary jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur refers to her as “one of Germany’s greatest jazz musicians,” while All About Jazz describes her piano style as “infinitely clever and classy.“ She has been nominated five times for the German Record Critics’ Award, including solo piano, chamber jazz, and jazz orchestra productions.

A central focus of her music is the trio with Fabian Timm on bass and Heinz Lichius on drums. Here, the orchestral dimension of her music becomes audible in a small format: compositions flow into one another, forming suite-like structures; extended arcs of tension move between intimacy and power; improvisations run through the pieces and intertwine with the written material.

As part of the series Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests, the trio opens with two concerts. Maria Baptist then expands the ensemble on separate evenings with Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger and Jan von Klewitz.

events.title: Practical Reflections on Intentional Kink Space Facilitation
events.description:
As Kink Space Facilitators, we experience a wide range of impressions in our work. We plan juicy offers, trauma and queer inclusive, and hold space for experiences, uncertainties, fuck ups, desires and much more. After planning and implementation comes reflection and evaluation. The ‘how was I’ as a professional and personally. 
Alexander Hahne, gay trans man, trainer and speaker for trans-specific topics in the field of sexual health, sex educator, somatic counselor, sexuality focussed bodyworker, systemic sex therapist, dancer and pleasure activist. Leader of workshops and individual counseling on the topics of body awareness, intimacy and sexuality. He works in the field of sexuality for about 20 years with almost 15 years of facilitation in pleasure and kink spaces. With his work he directly support them in their own experience of the body as well as the possibility of uncovering and using access to their own pleasurable potential. 
What happens in the workshop?
In this workshop, we will first put on our oxygen masks and subject our work to a reality check to see how it actually was. 
For example, we will address the following questions: 

Which methods worked really well and why?
Did the planning of your trauma-informed process have the desired effect during implementation?
Were there situations in which you felt uncertain or overwhelmed? What did you do then? What could be different next time?
Which methods did you use and why? What worked, what didn’t and why?

Yes, there is always too little time and the physical space is different than expected… how do you deal with that? How does that affect your stress level and facilitation? 
The approach is to separate your behaviour from you as a person. You as a person are highly valued and your behaviour is criticised. 
Note
This offering connects to and extends Ceci Ferox’s workshops Intentional Kink Space Facilitation and Intentional Kink Spaces: Structures and Organizing. You can purchase the recordings in our shop. If you did not have the opportunity to be part of these classes, we are offering the recordings for you to purchase as well. The recordings will be available until July 16th, 2026. This is optional, not mandatory. If you were part of one or both of these workshops, you can email us and get free access to the recordings again, if you purchase a ticket to this class.

events.title: Hurt Me, Deliciously
events.description:
There is something extraordinarily powerful in feeling and playing with consensual and voluntary pain. Why would a person want to feel pain? Why would another love to give it to someone else? How is pain and the processing of it changed depending on the context and relation it is put into? 
In the workshop, Mamana will go into a deep deep deep dive into all things pain and pain play. Together we will look at what pain actually is, how it is produced and interpreted in the brain and how it is influenced by personal, biological, social, and other contextual factors you can play with. We will go into the details of why people like to give and receive pain, how you can process it, which typical impact play instruments are helpful in inducing a certain kind of painful sensation. 
In short, this class will fry your brain with nerdy knowledge and allow you to think about your interest in pain play on a whole new level. Come for the facts, stay for the soul-searching of why sadomasochism is fucking delicious. 
What we will discuss

Define Pain?
Good pain, bad pain?
What do consent, trust and context have to do with it?
How to receive and process pain
How to tweak your pain play to where you want it to go
Why the fuck are we doing this?
many other little info tid-bits you will not see coming

events.title: Peter Gall Quintet
events.description:
Winner GERMAN JAZZ AWARD “ALBUM OF THE YEAR” 2025
Winner BMW Welt Jazz Award 2021
Peter Gall is not only one of the most renowned and in-demand German drummers of his generation; he has also made a name for himself as an outstanding composer and a thoughtful bandleader, looking beyond the rim of the drum in a refined and deeply personal way. In 2018, he released his album Paradox Dreambox, a powerful musical statement that received euphoric international acclaim and led to successful tours and festival appearances.
Now Peter Gall presents his second brilliant album LOVE AVATAR, which won the German Jazz Prize 2025 in the category “Album of the Year.” His new songs tell striking stories, paint dreamlike collages, and—with great atmospheric density—search for fascinating musical galaxies, emotional eruptions, and the magic and love inherent in music.
Joining him is an absolute “dream band”: Wanja Slavin, Carl Morgan, Rainer Böhm, and Matthias Pichler are among the influential crème de la crème of the young, dynamic, and innovative European jazz scene. Perfectly attuned to one another, this tightly knit ensemble forms a powerful musical unit. Their performances are gripping, highly virtuosic, and deeply emotional at the same time, unleashing an onstage energy that is almost impossible to resist—unsurprisingly, the Peter Gall Quintet won the prestigious BMW Welt Jazz Award in 2021.
A futuristic conglomerate of jazz, energetic fusion, anthemic indie spheres, beautiful melancholy, surprising grooves, and hypnotic beats captivates audiences and draws them into its spell.
„Perhaps we should briefly explain why the Peter Gall Quintet is currently one of the most interesting groups in Europe. (...) in which Afrobeat, Modern Jazz and EDM remain in the subtext and thus touch the subconscious. On this evening in the Unterfahrt, this doesn’t just work on stage, it spills over into the audience.“ Sueddeutsche Zeitung, Feuilleton
„The drummer’s second solo album has become a marvel of ‘new’ jazz. (...) [Peter Gall] and his first-class quintet weave a wide variety of jazz and non-jazz influences into an outrageously homogeneous album.“ MINT
„The album is dazzling“ Jazzwise
‚A new milestone from my favorite jazz drummer Peter Gall. An album of great energetic, atmospheric and playful density. Ten songs, ten stories.‘ Max Herre

events.title: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT SUMMERWEEKCONCERTS DAY4:<br>JAZZ VERSUS SOCCER<br>Maria Baptist Trio<br>Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests<br>FEAT TODAY: Fabian Timm-Heinz Lichius-Gabriel Coburger
events.description:
Maria Baptist Trio
Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests
FEAT TODAY: Fabian Timm-Heinz Lichius-Gabriel Coburger

Maria Baptist gehört zu den profiliertesten Pianistinnen und Komponistinnen des zeitgenössischen Jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur nennt sie »eine der großen Jazzmusikerinnen aus Deutschland«, All About Jazz beschreibt ihren Klavierstil als »unendlich intelligent und stilvoll«. Sie wurde fünf Mal für den Preis der Deutschen Schallplattenkritik nominiert, darunter für Soloklavier-, Kammerjazz- und Jazzorchester-Produktionen.

Ein zentraler Bezugspunkt ihrer Musik ist das Trio mit Fabian Timm am Bass und Heinz Lichius am Schlagzeug. Hier ist im kleinen Format das Großorchestrale ihres Werkkatalogs hörbar: Kompositionen fließen ineinander, formen suitenhafte Rahmen, weite Spannungsbögen wechseln zwischen Intimität und Kraft, Improvisationen durchziehen die Stücke und verweben sich mit dem Material.

In der Reihe Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests spielt das Trio zunächst zwei Konzerte. Danach erweitert Maria Baptist die Besetzung jeweils an einem eigenen Abend mit Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger und Jan von Klewitz.
—
Maria Baptist is one of the most distinctive pianists and composers in contemporary jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur refers to her as “one of Germany’s greatest jazz musicians,” while All About Jazz describes her piano style as “infinitely clever and classy.“ She has been nominated five times for the German Record Critics’ Award, including solo piano, chamber jazz, and jazz orchestra productions.

A central focus of her music is the trio with Fabian Timm on bass and Heinz Lichius on drums. Here, the orchestral dimension of her music becomes audible in a small format: compositions flow into one another, forming suite-like structures; extended arcs of tension move between intimacy and power; improvisations run through the pieces and intertwine with the written material.

As part of the series Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests, the trio opens with two concerts. Maria Baptist then expands the ensemble on separate evenings with Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger and Jan von Klewitz.

events.description: Spielerisch kämpfen  balgen wie als Kind  unbeschwert herumkugeln  raufen wie die Tierkinder  ausgelassen toben    Unter Anleitung und mit festen Regeln.    Jeden 2. und 4. Samstag im Monat  von 20-23:00h  (Einlass ab 16:45)    15€ an der Abendkasse, mit Reservierung per E-Mail 10€, <a href="mailto:info@playfight-xberg.de">info@playfight-xberg.de</a>, <a href="https://www.playfight-xberg.de" target="_blank" rel="noopener">www.playfight-xberg.de</a>    <strong>Aktuelles:</strong> Einladungslink zu unserem Telegram-Kanal für Termine, Neuigkeiten, und Änderungen (falls es mal welche gibt): <a href="https://t.me/+lNpr9L9e-mc5Nzky" target="_blank">https://t.me/+lNpr9L9e-mc5Nzky</a>    <strong>Und worum geht’s im playfight xberg?</strong>    Playfight bringt kreative Ideen und ausgelassenes Spielen mit achtsamem Kämpfen in einer sicheren und respektvollen Umgebung zusammen.  Wir kämpfen miteinander und nicht gegeneinander.  Es geht uns ums Spaß haben und nicht ums besiegen.  Wir setzen unsere Kräfte ein ohne verletzen zu wollen.  Vorsichtig, spielerisch, kräftiger, ausgelassen, achtsam.  Bei uns wird viel gelacht.  Playfight macht Spaß – und manchmal sogar ein deutliches Glücksgefühl.  Vorerfahrung im Kämpfen oder besondere sportliche Fitness ist nicht erforderlich.  Faire MitspielerInnen sind uns herzlich willkommen.  Wir nehmen aufeinander Rücksicht und begegnen einander mit Respekt und Neugierde.  Es geht uns um Körperkontakt ohne sexuellen Kontext, um Bewegung und darum intensiven Spaß zu haben.    <strong>Regeln</strong>    Wir playfighten maximal in Kniehöhe, um die Fallhöhe gering zu halten  Jede/r kann jederzeit STOP sagen oder 3 mal abklopfen. Die Situation wird damit sofort beendet.  Das bedeutet nicht unbedingt, dass der Kampf ganz abgebrochen werden muss, sondern man kann auch kurz stoppen und die Lage klären.  Ausdrücklich verboten sind Kampftechniken, deren Zweck es ist, zu verletzen, also KEIN Würgen, Treten, Schlagen, Hebeln, Beißen, festes Haare ziehen…    Vor einem Kampf können Vorabspachen über spezielle Wünsche oder/und persönliche Empfindlichkeiten getroffen werden.  Ihr könnt aber auch einfach schauen, welche Dynamik sich zwischen euch entwickelt, man kann sich auch während des Spielens weiter absprechen, und ansonsten kann man im Zweifelsfall ja jederzeit einfach „STOP“ sagen und die Situation klären.    <strong>Ablauf</strong>    <em>Aufwärmen und Kurzworkshop</em>    • wir aktivieren unseren unseren Körper mit verschiedenen Übungen  • üben praktisch ein, die eigenen Grenzen zu setzen und die des Grenzen des Partners zu respektieren  • probieren verschiedene Ideen aus wie man kämpfen kann  • machen ein kleine Roll- und Fallschule  • und lernen uns dabei natürlich schon ein bisschen kennen    <em>Hauptteil</em>    Zum Kämpfen treffen sich 2 Personen in der Mitte des Kreises.  KampfpartnerInnen können sich auf verschiedene Art finden.  Wer aufgefordert wird und nicht möchte, sagt oder signalisiert einfach „Nein“, ohne dass das nein begründet werden muss.  Die anderen TeilnehmerInnen bilden den Außenkreis und beobachten den Kampf und helfen dadurch einen sicheren Raum zu schaffen.    <strong>Bitte beachten:</strong>    • Schmuck bitte ablegen oder abkleben  • du solltest unbedingt etwas zu trinken (oder eine leere Flasche für Leitungswasser) mitbringen.  • unsere Bodenmatten sind in Hinsicht Hautabschürfungen ziemlich harmlos, aber um ganz sicher zu sein dass du sie vermeidest, bring am besten langärmlige und -beinige Kleidung und Socken mit.  Vorerfahrung oder besondere sportliche Fitness ist nicht erforderlich.    <strong>Außerdem gilt noch:</strong>    Playfight ist Sport.  Blaue Flecken und Abschürfungen sind beim playfight normal.  Größere Verletzungen kommen extrem selten vor.  Wir übernehmen keine Haftung, jede/r nimmt auf eigene Verantwortung teil.    Infos zu den Räumlichkeiten und zum Host Ulf findet ihr auf der homepage.    We are a safe space for LGBTQ+ and everyone else.

events.title: Rope Fundamentals Weekend: Foundations & Fun
events.description:
This is the Saturday single ticket event. For buying a full weekend ticket, go to the weekend event. 
Saturday gives you the tools that make shibari fun — or intense, or meditative, or horny, or whatever flavor of rope you want to create. Ceci will get you started with the most essential techniques: the lark’s head, the single column tie, clean wrapping, managing tension, and staying safe. Once those basics are in place, we spend the rest of the day putting them to use in playful, intuitive ways. 
We’ll explore freestyle tying and improvisation to loosen the pressure of “doing it right.” Through one-rope exercises, wrapping, unwrapping, and re-wrapping bodies, you’ll learn to follow curiosity instead of memorizing patterns. Because rope isn’t static — people move — we’ll also practice guiding and responding to movement through levers, spirals, and simple transitions like sitting to standing or shifting limbs mid-tie. 
Along the way, we dive into the emotional and psychological effects of rope: how body positions, pacing, tension, and proximity can shift headspace and shape intention. With just a few simple ties, you’ll learn to create sessions that feel impactful, intimate, and expressive. 
Take aways: 

Larkshead & single column tie
Rope safety
One rope tying, wrapping & unwrapping
Playing with different intentions and moods
Moving bodies & tying in movement

events.title: Rope Fundamentals: Shibari Starter Kit Weekend
events.description:
Kick off your rope journey with a weekend that bundles our entire Rope Fundamentals series into one playful, beginner-friendly shibari workshop. 
Across two days, you’ll move from the simplest building blocks to a clear understanding of how harnesses work. Whether you’re brand new, brushing off old skills, or craving a solid base before exploring deeper techniques, this weekend is designed to set you up with confidence, creativity, and connection. 
You can bring someone to tie with or come solo and find a partner at the workshop. 
Join us for the full journey, or pick the day that suits you best: 
Get Your Saturday (Foundations & Fun), only ticket here.
Get your Sunday (Nerdery & Harnesses), only ticket here. 
Foundations & Fun
Saturday gives you the tools that make shibari fun — or intense, or meditative, or horny, or whatever flavor of rope you want to create. Ceci will get you started with the most essential techniques: the lark’s head, the single column tie, clean wrapping, managing tension, and staying safe. Once those basics are in place, we spend the rest of the day putting them to use in playful, intuitive ways. 
We’ll explore freestyle tying and improvisation to loosen the pressure of “doing it right.” Through one-rope exercises, wrapping, unwrapping, and re-wrapping bodies, you’ll learn to follow curiosity instead of memorizing patterns. Because rope isn’t static — people move — we’ll also practice guiding and responding to movement through levers, spirals, and simple transitions like sitting to standing or shifting limbs mid-tie. 
Along the way, we dive into the emotional and psychological effects of rope: how body positions, pacing, tension, and proximity can shift headspace and shape intention. With just a few simple ties, you’ll learn to create sessions that feel impactful, intimate, and expressive. 
Take aways:

Larkshead & single column tie
Rope safety
One rope tying, wrapping & unwrapping
Playing with different intentions and moods
Moving bodies & tying in movement

Nerdery & Harnesses
Sunday is for the rope nerds (or for anyone ready to become one). Today we dive into the mechanics behind stable, comfortable, body-friendly tying. We’ll explore how to apply rope with intention, how to create structures that fit real bodies, and how to make your tying smoother, safer, and more efficient. 
You’ll learn counter tensions, ladder structures, your first frictions, and how to wrap with flow and consistency. These building blocks are what allow harnesses to hold their shape. We’ll also cover ergonomics and hand techniques, like hooking and pulling rope, so you can tie for longer without soreness or strain. 
With these tools in place, we’ll begin tying simple harnesses and, more importantly, understanding why they work. You’ll get a clear picture of the core components (anchors, stems, wraps, frictions, and cinches) and start recognizing the logic behind shibari structures. This modular thinking becomes the foundation for everything that comes after. 
Take aways:

Double column tie
Rope handling & ergonomics
Tension, counter tension & ladders
Intro to harnesses: anchors, stems, wraps, frictions, cinches
Frictions: Half hitch, full stop, munter hitch, in-line single column tie
One rope harnesses: chest harness, futomomo, box tie

events.title: Bondarev/Downes/Ginsburg/Michel
events.description:
Live at Donau115, the Bondarev / Downes / Ginsburg / Michel Band brings together four distinctive voices from the European improvised music scene for an evening of adventurous contemporary jazz, deep interaction, and spontaneous musical storytelling. Trumpeter Dima Bondarev’s lyrical intensity meets the harmonic imagination of pianist Kit Downes, grounded by the elastic groove and sensitivity of bassist Josh Ginsburg and drummer Marc Michel. Moving fluidly between original compositions, free improvisation, and modern jazz language, the quartet creates music that is both intimate and expansive — full of texture, risk, and collective energy.
Artist Bio
Dima Bondarev is one of the emerging voices of contemporary European jazz, known for a sound that combines lyrical depth, rhythmic urgency, and fearless improvisation. A graduate of Jazz Institut Berlin and former participant in the Focusyear program in Basel, he has collaborated with artists including Aaron Parks, Kit Downes, Gilad Hekselman, Kurt Rosenwinkel, Lionel Loueke, Joey Baron, Jorge Rossy, Jim Black and Wolfgang Muthspiel.
Kit Downes is internationally acclaimed for his deeply expressive approach to piano and improvisation, working across jazz, contemporary classical, and experimental music. His collaborations span an extensive range of leading European improvisers and ensembles.
Josh Ginsburg is an in-demand bassist and improviser whose playing is noted for its warmth, flexibility, and strong melodic sensibility within adventurous contemporary jazz settings.
Marc Michel is recognized for his dynamic, highly interactive drumming and broad stylistic range, performing with many leading musicians on the European jazz scene.

events.title: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT SUMMERWEEKCONCERTS DAY5:<br>JAZZ VERSUS SOCCER<br>Maria Baptist Trio<br>Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests<br>FEAT TODAY: Fabian Timm-Heinz Lichius-Jan von Klewitz
events.description:
Maria Baptist Trio
Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests
FEAT TODAY: Fabian Timm-Heinz Lichius-Jan von Klewitz

Maria Baptist gehört zu den profiliertesten Pianistinnen und Komponistinnen des zeitgenössischen Jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur nennt sie »eine der großen Jazzmusikerinnen aus Deutschland«, All About Jazz beschreibt ihren Klavierstil als »unendlich intelligent und stilvoll«. Sie wurde fünf Mal für den Preis der Deutschen Schallplattenkritik nominiert, darunter für Soloklavier-, Kammerjazz- und Jazzorchester-Produktionen.

Ein zentraler Bezugspunkt ihrer Musik ist das Trio mit Fabian Timm am Bass und Heinz Lichius am Schlagzeug. Hier ist im kleinen Format das Großorchestrale ihres Werkkatalogs hörbar: Kompositionen fließen ineinander, formen suitenhafte Rahmen, weite Spannungsbögen wechseln zwischen Intimität und Kraft, Improvisationen durchziehen die Stücke und verweben sich mit dem Material.

In der Reihe Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests spielt das Trio zunächst zwei Konzerte. Danach erweitert Maria Baptist die Besetzung jeweils an einem eigenen Abend mit Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger und Jan von Klewitz.
—
Maria Baptist is one of the most distinctive pianists and composers in contemporary jazz. Deutschlandfunk Kultur refers to her as “one of Germany’s greatest jazz musicians,” while All About Jazz describes her piano style as “infinitely clever and classy.“ She has been nominated five times for the German Record Critics’ Award, including solo piano, chamber jazz, and jazz orchestra productions.

A central focus of her music is the trio with Fabian Timm on bass and Heinz Lichius on drums. Here, the orchestral dimension of her music becomes audible in a small format: compositions flow into one another, forming suite-like structures; extended arcs of tension move between intimacy and power; improvisations run through the pieces and intertwine with the written material.

As part of the series Five Special Nights: Trio & Guests, the trio opens with two concerts. Maria Baptist then expands the ensemble on separate evenings with Philip Sindy, Gabriel Coburger and Jan von Klewitz.

events.title: Rope Fundamentals Weekend: Nerdery & Harnesses
events.description:
This is the Sunday single ticket event. For buying a full weekend ticket, go to the weekend event. 
Sunday is for the rope nerds (or for anyone ready to become one). Today we dive into the mechanics behind stable, comfortable, body-friendly tying. We’ll explore how to apply rope with intention, how to create structures that fit real bodies, and how to make your tying smoother, safer, and more efficient. 
You’ll learn counter tensions, ladder structures, your first frictions, and how to wrap with flow and consistency. These building blocks are what allow harnesses to hold their shape. We’ll also cover ergonomics and hand techniques, like hooking and pulling rope, so you can tie for longer without soreness or strain. 
With these tools in place, we’ll begin tying simple harnesses and, more importantly, understanding why they work. You’ll get a clear picture of the core components (anchors, stems, wraps, frictions, and cinches) and start recognizing the logic behind shibari structures. This modular thinking becomes the foundation for everything that comes after. 
Take aways: 

Double column tie
Rope handling & ergonomics
Tension, counter tension & ladders
Intro to harnesses: anchors, stems, wraps, frictions, cinches
Frictions: Half hitch, full stop, munter hitch, in-line single column tie
One rope harnesses: chest harness, futomomo, box tie

If you are not sure you can come, please purchase your ticket on the day as soon as you are absolutely sure you can make it.    <strong>Event Details</strong>    Date & Time: every Monday, 7 pm - 10 pm CET (Berlin)  Format: hands-on workshop  Audience: LGBTQIA+ & FRIENDS  Language: English  Minimum Knowledge Level: –  What to Bring: comfortable clothes that are more tight fitting if possible  Solo or Partnered: solo, partnered, in a group (everyone needs a ticket)    Price: 25-35 Euros    <strong>What we teach</strong>    – single column tie  – tension  – wrapping  – double column tie  – history of Japanese (inspired) rope bondage  - little bits of safety, anatomy and psychological care  - we will tie and play, yippie    <strong>What happens next?</strong>    If you like what you are being taught, we recommend repeating this class one or two more times so that you can develop muscle memory and a firmer understanding. Every last Monday of the month we also offer an adjacent class for absolute beginners that will go into the depth of learning about consent, boundaries, and negotiation as well as physical and psychological safety in ropes. Once you feel solid in your absolute basic skills and have joined the consent & safety class once, you are very welcome to move on to our Open Training for Beginners (also weekly on Monday).    <strong>Accessibility Note</strong>    The workshop is held in spoken English. German can also be provided. The space, KARA, is on the ground floor but has three steps to enter the house. A ramp for wheelchairs is available at all times. There is also a parking space available right in front of the door if needed. KARA has an accessible bathroom available. There are no thresholds in the entire house. The garden is only partially accessible at the moment. During the workshop, we will sit on the floor. Sitting in a chair can also be provided. Adaptations for physical needs will be shown and can also be provided upon request. If you participate in this workshop and need more assistance please message us at <a class="underline color-inherit hover-color-inherit" href="mailto:info@karada-house.de" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">info@karada-house.de</a> beforehand.    <strong>Who is this event for?</strong>    LGBTQIA+ describes the full spectrum of non-mainstream sexual orientation and/or gender identity, meaning: lesbian, gay, bisexual, pansexual, transgender, non-binary, genderqueer/fluid,    Friends describe people of any and all kinds of gender and sexual identities who are aware and respectful of the necessity, needs, and boundaries of a queer safe(r) space and its marginalized community.    When you consider yourself a friend you show acknowledgment to and are respectful of everyone’s self-expression and do not assume presume or project non-consensual ideas onto others. You actively request and use people’s chosen pronouns. You remain mindful of the fact that Karada House is first and foremost a space for queer people that you are also invited to attend. You have a genuine concern for the well-being of LGBTQIA+ people and remain in awareness of heterosexual and gender-straight privileges.    Friends don’t have to be perfect. None of us are. We request that we all proactively work and strive to be good friends and allies to marginalized people.    <strong>What else to know</strong>    If you cannot afford this event, please check the ticket option “solidarity” for reduced ticket prices. If that is still too much or they are out of stock, feel free to send us a message via <a class="underline text-inherit hover:text-inherit" href="mailto:info@karada-house.de" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">info@karada-house.de</a>    Before purchasing a <strong>solidarity ticket</strong>, please <a href="https://karada-house.de/faq/#solidarity" target="_blank" rel="noopener">check here if you are eligible for one</a>.

What we do

We show you the tools are we using and tell you why they are designed the way they are.
We talk about why people love to tie/get tied and what happens if you tie/get tied?
We show you the fundamental principles of shibari and first techniques you can immediately use
We talk about the history of shibari, give you pointers on anatomy, psychology and safety
We will tie ourselves, other people (if you and they want to) and actually take time to try stuff out and play, play, play

all kinds of bodies (abled and non-abled), all gender expressions, all kinds of sexualities (including people on the ace-spectrum), all kind of brains (neurospicy or neurotypical, affected by trauma, etc.)
people coming solo or bringing a partner (or group), people who only want to tie their own bodies as well as people who want to tie/get tied by others

Der Abend ist als offenes Treffen gedacht: respektvoll, neugierig und ohne Druck. Unterschiedliche Perspektiven und Erfahrungen sind willkommen. Ziel ist es, voneinander zu lernen, Fragen stellen zu können und Gedanken zu teilen. events.title: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT ARTIST IN SUMMER RESIDENCY DAY1:<br>JAZZ VERSUS SOCCER<br>ERNST BIER NEW TRIO<br>«TRIPLE»<br>FEAT: Christian Müller-Tal Arditi AND GUESTS
events.description:
ERNST BIER NEW TRIO
«TRIPLE»
FEAT: Christian Müller-Tal Arditi

Deutsch
Triple ist ein neues Bandprojekt vom Schlagzeuger Ernst Bier, entstanden vor 5 Monaten im A-Trane.
Im April spielten der  Gitarrist Tal Arditi, der Bassist Christian Müller und Ernst Bier zum zweiten Mal im Little Shop of Jazz von Ernst miteinander.
Die Chemie zwischen den Musikern stimmte sofort und das Publikum war sehr begeistert.
Das veranlasste die Musiker dazu ein neues Trio zu gründen und hier sind sie noch einmal!
Lassen Sie sich mitreißen von der ungeheuren Spiellaune dieser exzellenten Musiker. Sie leben mit und durch ihre Musik, eine Tatsache, die sie ausnahmslos mit viel Freude an die Zuhörer weitergeben.

Tal Arditi ist ein israelischer, in Berlin lebender Jazz-Gitarrist und Komponist. Anerkannt als junges Gitarrenwunder, begann Tal im Alter von 16 Jahren mit dem Studium im prestigeträchtigen „Jazzinstitut“ – Programm der „Rimon Music University“. Im Alter von 18 Jahren schloss er auf der renommierten Rimon School of Music in Ramat Hasharon in der Nähe von Tel Aviv erfolgreich mit einem Jazz-Diplom ab und beschloss nach Berlin zu ziehen.
In Berlin wurde Tal Arditi schnell zu einem der gefragtesten Musiker in der internationalen und lokalen Jazzszene und begann, regelmäßig in Clubs in ganz Europa sowie auf Festivals wie dem Umbria Jazz-Festival, dem Xjazz Festival, dem Red Sea Festival, dem Fusion Festival oder dem Open Air Keintal zu spielen.

Christian Müller ist Bassist und Komponist, der nach den Stationen Hamburg und Amsterdam, seit 2019 den Mittelpunkt seines Schaffens nach Berlin verlegt hat. Er studierte an der HfMT Hamburg sowie am Conservatorium van Amsterdam. Parallel dazu wurde er ins Bundesjazzorchester (BujazzO) unter der Leitung von Niels Klein und Jiggs Whigham aufgenommen. Konzertreisen führten ihn auf Bühnen in- und außerhalb Deutschlands. Unter anderem: Elbjazz-Festival (DE), Jazz Baltica-Festival(DE), Jazzkaar Festival (EST), Borneo Jazz Festival (MYS). In der Vergangenheit spielte er mit: John Schröder, Tony Malaby, Gilad Hekselmanm Seamus Blake, Marcio Doctor, Wanja Slavin, Ensemble Resonanz und noch vielen weiteren fabelhaften Musikerinnen. Christians Arbeit als Sideman ist auf mehreren Alben mit diversen Projekten dokumentiert. Ende 2025 kam sein Debütalbum „Golden Gloom“ heraus, welches ausschließlich Eigenkompositionen enthält.

Ernst Bier studierte Schlagzeug bei Billy Brooks, Charlie Persip, Vernell Fournier und Elvin Jones. Von 1983-1987 lebte und arbeitete er in NY-City. Nach seiner Rückkehr aus den Staaten lebte Ernst zunächst bei Köln und dann ab 1992 in Berlin. Die Liste der Musiker, mit denen er gearbeitet hat, liest sich wie ein Who’s Who des Jazz. Mit seinem einfühlsamen Spiel, seiner Hingabe und seiner konstruktiven Art hat er sich zu einem hochgeschätzten und gefragten Schlagzeuger entwickelt.

English
Triple is a new band project by drummer Ernst Bier, formed two months ago at the A-Trane jazz club.
In April, guitarist Tal Arditi, bassist Christian Müller, and Ernst Bier played together for the second time in Ernst’s Little Shop of Jazz.
The chemistry between the three musicians clicked immediately, and the audience was thrilled.
This prompted the musicians to form a new trio, and here they are again!
Let yourself be swept away by the incredible energy of these excellent musicians. They live with and through their music, a passion they consistently share with their audience with great joy.

Tal Arditi is an Israeli jazz guitarist and composer living in Berlin. Recognized as a young guitar prodigy, Tal began studying at the prestigious “Jazz Institute” program at Rimon Music University at the age of 16. At the age of 18, he successfully graduated with a jazz diploma from the renowned Rimon School of Music in Ramat Hasharon near Tel Aviv and decided to move to Berlin.
In Berlin, Tal Arditi quickly became one of the most sought-after musicians on the international and local jazz scene and began playing regularly in clubs throughout Europe as well as at festivals such as the Umbria Jazz Festival, the Xjazz Festival, the Red Sea Festival, the Fusion Festival, and the Open Air Keintal.

Christian Müller is a bassist and composer who, after spending time in Hamburg and Amsterdam, moved his creative center to Berlin in 2019. He studied at the HfMT Hamburg and the Conservatorium van Amsterdam. At the same time, he was accepted into the Bundesjazzorchester (BujazzO) under the direction of Niels Klein and Jiggs Whigham. Concert tours have taken him to stages in Germany and abroad. Among others: Elbjazz Festival (DE), Jazz Baltica Festival (DE), Jazzkaar Festival (EST), Borneo Jazz Festival (MYS). In the past, he has played with John Schröder, Tony Malaby, Gilad Hekselman, Seamus Blake, Marcio Doctor, Wanja Slavin, Ensemble Resonanz, and many other fabulous musicians. Christian’s work as a sideman is documented on several albums with various projects. At the end of 2025, his debut album “Golden Gloom” was released, which contains exclusively his own compositions.

Ernst Bier studied percussion with Billy Brooks, Charlie Persip, Vernell Fournier, and Elvin Jones. From 1983 to 1987, he lived and worked in New York City. After returning from the United States, Ernst first lived near Cologne and then, from 1992, in Berlin. The list of musicians he has worked with reads like a who’s who of jazz. With his sensitive playing, dedication, and constructive approach, he has become a highly regarded and sought-after drummer.

Tal Arditi – Guitar
Christian Müller – Bass
Ernst Bier – Drums

events.title: Tee:Trio + Sophie Link
events.description:
The singer Sophie Link views her voice not only as a melodic instrument, but continually explores its expressive potential at the intersection of improvisation, composition, and the spoken word.

The Tee.Trio is the working band of saxophonist Peter Ehwald. Born in Berlin, he has long been part of the local jazz scene and yet his work with musicians such as Tom Rainey, Robert Lanfermann and Laura Robles radiates beyond the borders of the City. The twins Andreas and Matthias Pichler play bass and drums with him. Matthias is highly virtuosic on bass and Andreas is theatrical and performative on drums.

For the three of them, the combination of jazz and modernity is part of his everyday music-making. Following their regular engagement at Berlin's Tee.Salon:iki, their release “Live in Berlin” will appear in the spring – a concert recording from the B-Flat jazz club. The Tee.Trio's concerts develop an improvisational pull in which anything is possible thanks to their irrepressible joy of playing—jazz tradition, heartbreaking ballads, folklore from Tyrol, and a sky-high search for freedom.

events.title: Domingo Fantástico #7
events.description:
I am pleased to present a new edition of Domingo Fantástico, a music and variety show series held at Donau115. Inspired by the great weekend television shows that shaped generations across Latin America and Spain, this event celebrates the diversity and creativity of the Spanish-speaking community in Berlin.

In this edition, we will travel through Mexico with three musical projects that, from different perspectives and artistic paths, keep alive the connection between tradition, identity, and contemporary creation.

The evening will feature Frieda, a singer, songwriter, and producer from Mexico City whose music embodies the spirit of neo-Mexicanity, bringing together Mexican folklore and contemporary songwriting. In an intimate acoustic format, she will present songs that connect Mexico and Europe through stories, emotions, and memory.

We will also welcome Sauceedo, a musician from Monterrey, for whom creating music is a way to experience flow and peace of mind, sharing songs born from a sincere and personal artistic journey.

Completing the line-up is El Cuervo del Norte from Guadalajara, presenting a repertoire of regional Mexican music inspired by the tradition of the corrido, where popular stories, legends, and reflections on life and death come together.

An evening dedicated to the richness and diversity of Mexican music, celebrating its roots and its presence within Berlin’s cultural scene.

events.description:
A new quartet exploring original compositions and improvisation, with musicians based in New York and Berlin.

Pianist and composer Álvaro Torres is an emerging voice in New York City's creative jazz scene. His life has been shaped by an international trajectory, leading him to live in a variety of places such as Kathmandu, Barcelona, Copenhagen, and Berlin, experiences that have profoundly influenced his music. Álvaro has released five albums as a leader for record labels like Sunnyside Records and Fresh Sound New Talent, featuring notable collaborations with musicians such as Barry Altschul, Tony Malaby, Francisco Mela, Nasheet Waits, John Hébert, and Kresten Osgood. His music blends post-bop and improvisation, drawing from elements of Spanish folklore and his strong classical music background.

"Artfully unpredictable…Extraordinary" — All About Jazz

“Torres’ compositions pull in influences from post- bop to Spanish folklore, but always remain direct and accessible, with a swinging core”— New York City Jazz Record

"One of the most promising future stars of the genre" — La Razón

events.description:
RELEASE CONCERT 'AND ALL I HAVE TO GIVE'

PHOENIX LOVE is the new band project of singer and composer Dora Osterloh.

The music combines concrete song elements with free improvisation and personal-abstract lyrics. Dora Osterloh, Theresia Philipp, Keisuke Matsuno, Simon Jermyn and Lukas Akintaya are creative players in the Cologne and Berlin jazz scene and can be experienced in various constellations and bands. With PHOENIX LOVE they form an independent ensemble, which brings both the free-spirited playing attitude of improvisation and emotional empathy to the compositions and lyrics. Dora Osterloh’s voice moves playfully between instrumental, noisy and singing expression. This creates an extraordinary band sound, characterized by rhythmic complexity, melodic and harmonic depth and spherical soundscapes.

PHOENIX LOVE’s first album And All I Have to Give will be released on July 3, 2026 on Boomslang Records.

events.title: Alden Hellmuth 'Tether'
events.description:
Bio:
Alden Hellmuth is a saxophonist, composer, and improviser based in New York City. A graduate of the Herbie Hancock Institute, she received the 2025 German Jazz Prize for Debut Album of the Year (International) for her album Good Intentions (Fresh Sound Records) and has performed internationally at major venues and festivals including the NYC Winter Jazz Festival, Hollywood Bowl and Blue Note Jazz Festival, International Jazz Day (Morocco and Abu Dhabi), The Jazz Gallery, and Blue Note NYC. Alden has been recognized with numerous honors, including New Music USA’s Next Jazz Legacy (2026), Chamber Music America’s Performance Plus Grant (2025), ASCAP’s Herb Alpert Young Jazz Composer Award (2024), and the Focusyear Fellowship (2021-22). As an artist, Alden seeks expression through freedom, intuition, and a deep commitment to her craft. 

She'll be presenting music from her newest project, Tether, set to be released June 26th with Berlin-based record label Leiter Verlag, with NYC band Yvonne Rogers on piano, Timothy Angulo on drums, and Phil Donkin on bass.

Another Tether:
Alden Hellmuth’s Tether is a quartet that leans hard into density, motion, and low-end gravity. Developed during her time in Los Angeles, the project explores a striking array of moods, tones, and textures with intensity and unmistakable momentum. With her "challenging and evocative" (Jazz Times) compositional vision and a sharp improvisational language, Hellmuth has carefully and creatively crafted a new sonic realm using the distinct voices in her band. The recorded work, Hellmuth's sophomore release, features Los Angeles bassists Logan Kane and Miller Wrenn, acclaimed drummer Justin Brown, and appearances by pianist Paul Cornish and trumpeter Yakiv Tsvietinskyi. Out June 26th on Berlin-based label Leiter, Tether is a bold statement of intent.

Facebook Andreas Schmidt

It´s me, the Monday A-Trane pianist Andreas Schmidt. Since 1995 I played here about 900 wonderful & surprising improvised happenings in music with lots of friends like Jay Clayton, Hayden Chisholm, Dave Douglas, Walter Norris, Mark Murphy, Till Brönner, Sebastian Merk, Andreas Edelmann, Jan Roder, Connie Crothers, Max Andrzejewski, Andy Fite etc.. Here’s what Richard Williams wrote about me in his blog: «If you’re ever at a loose end in Berlin on a Monday night, my advice would be to head for A-Trane, the jazz club in Charlottenburg, where Andreas Schmidt, a pianist, composer and teacher at the city’s Jazz Institut, holds a weekly free-admission session featuring a changing cast. Schmidt is a fine pianist, the salient features of his playing located somewhere between the Paul Bley of the mid-’60s and the Chick Corea of «Now He Sings, Now He Sobs». You might get an idea of his approach if I say that his first album was made (in 1995) with Lee Konitz, and a later one comprised a duo with Gary Peacock. His music is cerebral, but on the evidence I’ve heard it never lacks wit and humanity.» Richard Williams

Andreas Schmidt, Piano

events.title: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT JAZZ VERSUS SOCCER A Summer Residency DAY1:<br>JUDY NIEMACK<br>«SINGING MILES»<br>100 YEARS MILES<br>FEAT: Dima Bondarev-Yuriy Seredin-Doug Weiss-Marc Michel
events.description:
JUDY NIEMACK
«SINGING MILES»
100 YEARS MILES
FEAT: Dima Bondarev-Yuriy Seredin-Doug Weiss-Marc Michel

ENGLISH:
This week at A-Trane, acclaimed jazz vocalist and educator Judy Niemack presents Singing Miles—a special vocal celebration of the music associated with the legendary trumpeter Miles Davis. Joined by various guest trumpet artists from the Berlin jazz scene, Niemack reimagines Miles’s repertoire through voice, improvisation, and personal musical expression. Singing Miles explores the lyricism, mystery, and innovation that defined Davis’s artistry, bringing together intimate ballads, swinging classics, and adventurous jazz repertoire in a vibrant and contemporary concert experience.

Jazz critic Neil Tesser wrote in DownBeat about Niemack: “You sing like an angel, or at least an angel who’s heard Basie and Miles: you’ve got intonation that whole choruses would kill for, and a voice that never loses its soft sheen even at hot tempos and high volume. You’re one of the few singers who actually should sing scat solos, since you think so much like a horn player.”

Join Judy Niemack for an unforgettable week at A-Trane, where the music of Miles Davis is brought to life anew with passion, imagination, and the inspiring voices of Berlin’s jazz trumpet community.

DEUTSCH:
Diese Woche präsentiert die gefeierte Jazzsängerin und Pädagogin Judy Niemack im A-Trane Singing Miles – eine besondere vokale Hommage an die Musik des legendären Trompeters Miles Davis. Gemeinsam mit wechselnden Gasttrompetern der Berliner Jazzszene interpretiert Niemack das mit Miles Davis verbundene Repertoire neu – mit Stimme, Improvisation und persönlicher musikalischer Handschrift. Singing Miles erkundet die Lyrik, Spannung und Innovationskraft, die Davis’ Kunst prägten, und verbindet intime Balladen mit swingenden und abenteuerlichen Jazzklassikern zu einem lebendigen und zeitgenössischen Konzerterlebnis.

Der Jazzkritiker Neil Tesser schrieb im DownBeat über Judy Niemack: „Du singst wie ein Engel – oder zumindest wie ein Engel, der Basie und Miles gehört hat: mit einer Intonation, um die dich ganze Chöre beneiden würden, und einer Stimme, die selbst bei schnellen Tempi und großer Dynamik ihren weichen Glanz bewahrt. Du gehörst zu den wenigen Sängerinnen, die tatsächlich Scat-Soli singen sollten, weil du so sehr wie ein Bläser denkst.“

Erleben Sie eine unvergessliche Woche im A-Trane, in der die Musik von Miles Davis mit Leidenschaft, Fantasie und der inspirierenden Klangwelt der Berliner Jazzszene neu zum Leben erweckt wird.

Judy Niemack – Vocal
Yuriy Seredin – Piano
Marc Michel – Drums
Dima Bondarev – Trumpet
Doug Weiss – Bass

FocusYear Band
events.description:
Focusyear Band 26

EN
This year’s Focusyear Band takes shape as a quintet of five strongly individual young musicians, each
bringing distinct backgrounds and influences into a shared artistic space. Their diversity generates a rich spectrum of musical colors and possibilities. What unites them is a deep engagement with both traditional and contemporary expressions of jazz and jazz-related music, and a strong commitment to the art of improvisation.

Swiss vocalist Alice Auclair combines a finely nuanced approach to song interpretation with harmonically informed improvisation, marked by a clear, magnetic voice and impressive intonation. Belgian guitarist Eliott Knuets stands out for his remarkable virtuosity and expressive range, revealing a musical maturity and rhythmic connectedness well beyond his years.

Australian pianist Wilbur Whitta brings exceptional rhythmic focus and architectural clarity, shaping solos that rise into moments of intensity and drive. Spanish bassist Eva Serrano forms the rhythmic and sonic foundation of the band with her pulse-oriented, resonant bass playing, while also expanding the ensemble’s texture through the use of her voice. 

Drummer Dae Bryant anchors and propels the group with a dynamic, soulful, and often poetic approach, continuously inventing new layers of accompaniment while responding in the moment to the sound of his fellow musicians.

During their year in Basel, these five musicians—selected from a large international pool of applicants—have taken part in an intensive program of coaching and performance. They have worked closely with an impressive group of internationally renowned jazz artists, including Allison Miller, Django Bates, Guillermo Klein, Ingrid Jensen, Ingrid Laubrock, Wolfgang Muthspiel, Kendrick Scott, Kris Davis, Lionel Loueke, Miguel Zenón, Jaleel Shaw, Michael Mayo, Mario Rom, Darcy James Argue, Linda May Han Oh, and Jonathan Blake. Focusyear Band 26 now presents a program of original music, written by all band members and developed throughout this year-long process—music that
is collective in spirit, interactive in form, and marked by intensity, openness, and a distinctly
contemporary voice.

DE
Die diesjährige Focusyear Band formiert sich als Quintett aus fünf stark eigenständigen jungen
Musiker:innen, die ihre unterschiedlichen Hintergrün- de und musikalischen Einflüsse in einen gemeinsamen künstlerischen Raum einbringen. Diese Vielfalt erzeugt ein reiches Spektrum an musikalischen Farben und Ausdrucksmöglichkeiten. Was sie verbindet, ist eine tiefe Auseinandersetzung mit sowohl traditionellen als auch zeitgenössischen Ausdrucksformen des Jazz und jazzverwandter Musik sowie ein starkes Bekenntnis zur Kunst der Improvisation.

Die Schweizer Sängerin Alice Auclair verbindet eine fein nuancierte Herangehensweise an die Interpretation von Songs mit harmonisch fundierter Improvisation, geprägt von einer klaren, magnetischen Stimme und beeindruckender Intonationssicherheit. 

Der belgische Gitarrist Eliott Knuets überzeugt durch aussergewöhnliche Virtuosität und Ausdruckskraft und zeigt eine musikalische Reife sowie rhythmische Verbundenheit weit über sein Alter hinaus. Der australische Pianist Wilbur Whitta bringt außergewöhnliche rhythmische Präzision
und architektonische Klarheit ein und gestaltet Soli, die sich zu Momenten großer Intensität und Energie steigern. Die spanische Bassistin Eva Serrano bildet mit ihrem pulsorientierten, resonanten Bassspiel das rhythmische und klangliche Fundament der Band und erweitert zugleich die Textur des Ensembles durch den Einsatz ihrer Stimme. Schlagzeuger Dae Bryant verankert und treibt
die Gruppe mit einem dynamischen, souligen und oft poetischen Ansatz voran, indem er fortlaufend neue Begleitebenen erfindet und im Moment auf den Klang seiner Mitmusiker reagiert.

Während ihres Jahres in Basel haben diese fünf Musiker:innen – ausgewählt aus einem großen internationalen Bewerberfeld – an einem intensiven Programm aus Coachings und Auftritten teilgenommen. Dabei arbeiteten sie eng mit einer beeindruckenden Gruppe international renommierter Jazzkünstler:innen zusammen, darunter Allison Miller, Django Bates, Guillermo Klein,

events.title: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT JAZZ VERSUS SOCCER A Summer Residency DAY2:<br>JUDY NIEMACK<br>«SINGING MILES»<br>100 YEARS MILES<br>FEAT: Florian Menzel-Yuriy Seredin-Doug Weiss-Marc Michel
events.description:
JUDY NIEMACK
«SINGING MILES»
100 YEARS MILES
FEAT: Florian Menzel-Yuriy Seredin-Doug Weiss-Marc Michel

ENGLISH:
This week at A-Trane, acclaimed jazz vocalist and educator Judy Niemack presents Singing Miles—a special vocal celebration of the music associated with the legendary trumpeter Miles Davis. Joined by various guest trumpet artists from the Berlin jazz scene, Niemack reimagines Miles’s repertoire through voice, improvisation, and personal musical expression. Singing Miles explores the lyricism, mystery, and innovation that defined Davis’s artistry, bringing together intimate ballads, swinging classics, and adventurous jazz repertoire in a vibrant and contemporary concert experience.

Jazz critic Neil Tesser wrote in DownBeat about Niemack: “You sing like an angel, or at least an angel who’s heard Basie and Miles: you’ve got intonation that whole choruses would kill for, and a voice that never loses its soft sheen even at hot tempos and high volume. You’re one of the few singers who actually should sing scat solos, since you think so much like a horn player.”

Join Judy Niemack for an unforgettable week at A-Trane, where the music of Miles Davis is brought to life anew with passion, imagination, and the inspiring voices of Berlin’s jazz trumpet community.

DEUTSCH:
Diese Woche präsentiert die gefeierte Jazzsängerin und Pädagogin Judy Niemack im A-Trane Singing Miles – eine besondere vokale Hommage an die Musik des legendären Trompeters Miles Davis. Gemeinsam mit wechselnden Gasttrompetern der Berliner Jazzszene interpretiert Niemack das mit Miles Davis verbundene Repertoire neu – mit Stimme, Improvisation und persönlicher musikalischer Handschrift. Singing Miles erkundet die Lyrik, Spannung und Innovationskraft, die Davis’ Kunst prägten, und verbindet intime Balladen mit swingenden und abenteuerlichen Jazzklassikern zu einem lebendigen und zeitgenössischen Konzerterlebnis.

Der Jazzkritiker Neil Tesser schrieb im DownBeat über Judy Niemack: „Du singst wie ein Engel – oder zumindest wie ein Engel, der Basie und Miles gehört hat: mit einer Intonation, um die dich ganze Chöre beneiden würden, und einer Stimme, die selbst bei schnellen Tempi und großer Dynamik ihren weichen Glanz bewahrt. Du gehörst zu den wenigen Sängerinnen, die tatsächlich Scat-Soli singen sollten, weil du so sehr wie ein Bläser denkst.“

Erleben Sie eine unvergessliche Woche im A-Trane, in der die Musik von Miles Davis mit Leidenschaft, Fantasie und der inspirierenden Klangwelt der Berliner Jazzszene neu zum Leben erweckt wird.

Judy Niemack – Vocal
Yuriy Seredin – Piano
Marc Michel – Drums
Florian Menzel – Trumpet
Doug Weiss – Bass

events.title: Mads Riis Quartet
events.description:
Rooted in jazz, our music weaves a tapestry of powerful, evocative melodies, ambient soundscapes, and minimalist aesthetics. It is an exploration of identity and belonging. At its core, the music stems from a longing to find one’s roots and a sense of grounding in a time marked by increasing uncertainty. The result is music that paints vivid portraits of the inner life, where nostalgia and hope converge. It often draws from places, memories, or relationships, hoping that the music will appeal to the listener, allowing them to relate and explore memories and emotions in their own way.

Mads Riis released his debut album in May 2026 on all streaming platforms - he was awarded the Karl Hofer Jazz-Stipendium in late-2025 for his compositions, where the jury stated: ”With his warm sound aesthetic and deeply emotional playing, Mads Riis impressed across the board. (…) As a composer and guitarist, he creates an intimate yet powerful musical language that impressively combines personal experiences and artistic maturity." 

He also won the first place in the Keep An Eye International Jazz Award final at BIMHUIS in april 2026 - playing his compositions with his group. This special perfomance will feature brand new songs and songs from the album.
